ledger.note: 424: the Dangchang Qiang kingdom's first dated record. 'The first recorded interaction was in 424, when Liang Mihu, grandson of Liang Qin, sent a petition to the Northern Wei', offering submission. Confidence 1: the page dates no founding ('c. 4th century' in the infobox; Liang Qin 'unified the Dangchang Qiang'), so 424 is the first dated mention, not the birth.

ledger.note: 564: Northern Zhou ends Dangchang. 'Northern Zhou launched a campaign after Liang Miding repeatedly raided their territory in 564', 'Dangchang fell that same year' and Dang province was set up there. Infobox 'Disestablished: 564'.

wars.name: Dangchang raids on Wei and Zhou
wars.outcome: 'In the 6th century, as the Northern Wei collapsed and split into two', Dangchang allied with the Tuyuhun and attacked the Northern Wei and then the Western Wei; Liang Miding's raids in 564 brought the Northern Zhou campaign that ended the kingdom.
wars.note: No year for the first raids; the page names no places. Dangchang paid tribute to Northern Wei, Liu Song, Southern Qi and Liang for titles and protection, undated.

certainty.note: A mountain kingdom described by one line of area; no frontier on any page.

sources.title: Dangchang Kingdom
sources.note: Whole state: infobox (c. 4th century to 564), area, capital, 424 petition, 6th-century raids, 564 fall, ruler table.

sources.title: Northern Zhou
sources.note: Searched for Dangchang, Dengzhi, Qiang, Tuyuhun, Wuxing, Yinping, Chouchi, Dang province: none named; the 564 campaign rests on the Dangchang page alone.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; the group scope asks for 'the Di and Qiang states' frontiers'. One page carries the whole state; the Liang Miding page failed (URL_NOT_FOUND) and the Northern Zhou page is silent on 564. Founding: 'c. 4th century' (infobox); the 424 start is the first dated mention. Rulers with an undated end are omitted from the strip. Dangchang's tribute and submission to the Northern Wei (424) and the southern dynasties are undated vassal relations for those dossiers to carry. Family set to steppe by analogy with tuyuhun; a Qiang colour family does not exist.
